reconcile.connective: Harmonizers read the letters as one revelation unfolding in stages: imminence in 1 Thessalonians never excluded the apostasy 2 Thessalonians says must come first.

discrepancy.connective: F. C. Baur pressed this very point to argue 1 Thessalonians' imminent hope and 2 Thessalonians' delayed timetable cannot come from the same author.

skeptic.name: F. C. Baur
skeptic.attribution: F. C. Baur, Paulus, der Apostel Jesu Christi (1845)

excerpts.excerpt_text: The Spirit subsequently revealed by Paul that which is not inconsistent with the expectation here taught of the Lord's coming at any time; namely, that His coming would not be until there should be a "falling away first" (Th2 2:2-3); but as symptoms of this soon appeared, none could say but that still this precursory event might be realized, and so the Lord come in his day.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: JFB directly harmonizes the imminence language of 1 Thess 4:15 with the 'falling away first' requirement of 2 Thess 2:2-3, framing both as stages of one progressive revelation rather than as a change of timetable.

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley treats this exact tension directly under 'His coming at hand' vs. 'Deferred and far off' (tabulating 1 Cor 15:51-52, Phil 4:5, 1 Thess 4:15, and 1 Pet 4:7 against 2 Thess 2:2-3), naming Baur's charge of contradiction and answering it by quoting De Wette, Davidson, and Andrew Fuller.
